required_units: The first delivered plan was direct at 0.000 m maximum lateral deviation, while later delivered plans had non-direct geometry.
The 70 delivered plans had 70 unique SHA-256 identities and ranged from -1.1749 m to +1.0351 m signed deviation about the requested line.
Delivered odometry also departed from the requested line, reaching 1.1042 m maximum lateral deviation, and NavigateToPose returned success after 73.110 s.
The available rolling costmap did not cover enough of the complete requested route to classify the physical trigger.
A delivered plan is not proof of controller consumption, and the record does not establish which observation or physical condition caused the plan changes.
The answer recommends time-aligning plan poses with complete costmap observations or adding planner/controller introspection before attributing a specific trigger.
prohibited_claims: A specific obstacle or retained costmap snapshot caused the plan changes.
Every delivered plan was followed or consumed by the controller.
A route update occurred after each metre of physical travel without an explicit time-aligned derivation.
The evaluator-only layout, seed, obstacle identity, or intended mechanism is method-visible evidence.
The episode establishes global route infeasibility or a navigation failure.
The BT event history is proven complete despite the unobserved terminal transition.

limits: The rolling costmap was incomplete for full requested-route classification.
Delivered plan geometry does not prove controller consumption.
Temporal association does not prove observation-to-plan causation.
Evaluator-only semantic geometry and obstacle identity are unavailable to methods.
The case is development-only, not held-out or confirmatory evidence.
